land.text: 'It is a successor of the Cemetery H culture and black and red ware culture (BRW) within this region' (Haryana, the Ghaggar-Hakra country)

predecessors.note: The Indus dossier (sa-01-a) draws the Late Harappan Haryana and Punjab to -1300 and gives them to nobody; the PGW infobox starts in -1200, so -1299..-1201 is a gap on the page's dates (Uesugi's chronology, 'from 1300', would close it).

land.text: the Ochre Coloured Pottery page says 'The OCP was succeeded by this culture' (Ganga-Yamuna country); no more precise land is given

predecessors.note: The PGW infobox also lists Ochre Coloured Pottery as a predecessor; that culture's infobox ends in -1500.

land.text: the Kuru country: Hastinapur and Bhagwanpura (Kurukshetra) are PGW sites, and the page says the culture 'probably corresponds to the middle and late Vedic period, i.e., the Kuru-Panchala kingdom'

successors.note: Reading of mine: the infobox says only 'Followed by: Mahajanapadas'.

land.text: Ahichchhatra, a major PGW site in Rohilkhand, the northern Panchala
Mathura, a PGW site of 'around 375 hectares'
Kosambi, a PGW site at the Ganga-Yamuna confluence

successors.note: Reading of mine; the page's Period III (c. 600-300 BCE) runs on after the Mahajanapada convention year.

correction.text: the Ghaggar valley and the upper Ganga region where 'it makes its appearance' in Uesugi's Period I: Haryana (Bhagwanpura in Kurukshetra district, Panipat), the upper Ganga around Hastinapur (Meerut) and the Rupnagar site on the Sutlej (Chandigarh 50 km stands in for it)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no PGW row). Infobox 'c. 1200-600 BCE'; Uesugi's Period I 'c. 1300-1000 BCE: when it makes its appearance in the Ghaggar valley and the upper Ganga region'. The page gives no area (its figures are in hectares: Mathura 'around 375 hectares'); the keyframe resolves to about 73,000 km2 and cannot be checked against an infobox figure.

correction.text: 'the western Gangetic plain and the Ghaggar-Hakra valley': Period II 'spreads into the western part of the Ganga valley', so Haryana, the Ganges-Yamuna Doab, Mathura, Ahichchhatra (Bareilly) and Kosambi (Allahabad), with Hastinapur and Rupnagar kept

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Uesugi's Period II 'c. 1000-600 BCE: when it spreads into the western part of the Ganga valley'; '1,576 PGW sites have been discovered' (as of 2018). The page names sites, not a boundary (the keyframe resolves to about 205,000 km2), so the shape is a union of named regions around the infobox sites (Hastinapur, Mathura, Ahichchhatra, Panipat, Rupnagar, Bhagwanpura, Kosambi). Period III (c. 600-300 BCE, 'with interactions to the east') runs beyond this dossier's end; it is not drawn.

region.text: the Ghaggar valley and the upper Ganga region where 'it makes its appearance' in Uesugi's Period I: Haryana (Bhagwanpura in Kurukshetra district, Panipat), the upper Ganga around Hastinapur (Meerut) and the Rupnagar site on the Sutlej (Chandigarh 50 km stands in for it)

ledger.note: c. 1200 BCE: the Painted Grey Ware culture appears in the Ghaggar valley and the upper Ganga region. Infobox 'c. 1200-600 BCE'; 'conventionally dated c.1200 to 600-500 BCE, or from 1300 to 500-300 BCE'; Uesugi's Period I (c. 1300-1000) 'when it makes its appearance in the Ghaggar valley and the upper Ganga region'. The year is the infobox's; the region is read from the named valley and river.

region.text: the western Ganga valley beyond the first keyframe: the Doab, Mathura, Ahichchhatra and Kosambi

ledger.note: c. 1000 BCE: the culture spreads east into the western Ganga valley. Uesugi's Period II 'c. 1000-600 BCE: when it spreads into the western part of the Ganga valley'; 'Towards the end of the period, many of the PGW settlements grew into the large towns and cities'.

region.text: the whole PGW country passes to the Mahajanapadas (Kuru, Panchala, Surasena, Vatsa and the rest)

ledger.note: c. 600 BCE: the Painted Grey Ware period gives way to the Mahajanapadas. Infobox 'c. 1200-600 BCE', 'Followed by: Mahajanapadas'; the page also has 'It is succeeded by Northern Black Polished Ware c. 700-500 BCE' and Uesugi's Period III runs to 300 BCE, so the end is the Mahajanapada convention year, not a hard break.

certainty.note: An archaeological culture known from sites ('1,576 PGW sites'), not from frontiers: every edge is an interpolation between named sites.

sources.title: Painted Grey Ware culture
sources.note: Identity, infobox 1200-600 BCE, Uesugi's three periods, site list, 'preceded by' and 'followed by', Kuru-Panchala correspondence.

sources.title: Ochre Coloured Pottery culture
sources.note: Only for the predecessor note: the OCP is succeeded by Painted Grey Ware; its infobox 'c. 2000-1500 BCE'.

notes: Type culture although the schema describes cultures before 3400 BCE: the Indus dossier (sa-01-a) uses the same convention to -1300, and the group scope asks for PGW as a post-Indus culture. The page gives no area, so no Cliopatria or infobox comparison is possible (there is no Cliopatria row). Overlap to expect: the Vedic Kuru and Panchala kingdoms (the page says the culture 'probably corresponds' to them) are drawn as states over this culture where a dossier exists (kuru-kingdom and panchala-kingdom in this batch); the renderer should let the state win. Chronology: the infobox dates 1200-600; the same page's 'from 1300 to 500-300 BCE' and Uesugi's Period I c. 1300 would close the 1300-1200 gap after the Indus dossier's -1300 end. Not drawn: BRW in central India (contemporary with PGW), Period III after -600, Northern Black Polished Ware. Gazetteer: Rupnagar (Ropar, Punjab, 30.97N 76.53E) is not a place; Chandigarh 50 km stands in for it.
